summary.name: Postmortem Action Items: Plan the Work and Work the Plan
summary.one_liner: A 2017 SREcon Americas talk by Google's Sue Lueder and Betsy Beyer on designing high-quality postmortem action items and making sure they get implemented.
use_cases: Designing action items after a production incident
Making sure postmortem follow-up work actually gets done
Balancing reliability fixes against competing priorities
Learning how Google approaches postmortem follow-through
summary.what_it_does: This is a conference talk page (SREcon17 Americas, USENIX, March 2017) rather than a software tool. The talk covers best practices for developing high-quality postmortem action items and methods for ensuring those items are implemented, so the same outage does not recur. It discusses doing this amid competing priorities, resource limits, and operational realities. The speakers state that Google teams are not perfect at this and present their thoughts as a starting point for industry discussion. Slides, video and audio are posted as open access per USENIX policy.
notable: Speakers are from Google's SRE team and build on the 2016 O'Reilly book Site Reliability Engineering
Covers both writing high-quality action items and executing them in practice
Hosted by USENIX with open access to papers, slides and recordings
caveats: The speakers acknowledge Google teams are not perfect at postmortem action items
Page text is a talk abstract; specific methods are not listed on the page
